title: Graceful warmup credit exchange and burst cooldown controller
author: Noah Carr
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while allowing short, network-safe bursts for traffic spikes. Current warm-pool semantics are binary (reserved vs ephemeral) and cause either wasted capacity or sudden noisy neighbor effects during bursts. This PR introduces a 'warmup credit exchange' broker and a 'burst cooldown controller' to permit controlled, graceful borrowing of reserved warm slots with automatic reconciliation and telemetry for debugging.

What this change does: Implements a broker that can (a) atomically transfer ephemeral warm credits from a tenant's reserved pool to its burstable allowance, (b) track and ledger transfers with idempotency keys so transfers can be reconciled after partial failures, and (c) support a lease-based model where credits time out if not observed in the runtime within a configurable lease window. Adds a cooldown controller that decays a tenant's burst budget on a configurable window and applies a soft-shed threshold when the tenant's negative balance exceeds a safety margin.

Motivation and tradeoffs: The exchange model favors availability and bounded latency for short spikes at the cost of small temporary overcommit; the cooldown controller prevents oscillation and long-term SLA erosion. We chose lease-based credits (instead of permanent re-reservation) so normal reserved capacity accounting is preserved and failures (eg. node crashes) can be reconciled quickly without manual intervention.

Checklist:
- [x] Broker and controller implementation with unit tests
- [x] E2E test harness for warmup flows simulating prewarm, burst, node eviction
- [x] Telemetry hooks (p50/p95 headroom gauges, credit-transfer counters, failed-reconcile alerts)
- [x] Runbook + operational notes in docs/runbooks/dedicated/warmup_and_burst.md
- [x] Backwards-compatible config (default behavior unchanged unless enabled)

Operational knobs added: warmup_credit_lease_seconds (default 60), burst_cooldown_decay_seconds (default 30, configurable), safety_negative_balance_ratio (default 0.3), enable_credit_exchange (off by default).

Testing notes: e2e harness runs simulated spike workloads and eviction events; CI initially flagged a flaky e2e test (race on credit reconciliation). I added an explicit reconciliation backoff and a deterministic clock in tests; CI green after re-run. Load test against a 200-node dedicated cluster shows 9-13% reduction in p99 token latency during spikes and <2% increase in steady-state reserved utilization for tenants that borrowed credits.

Rollout plan: feature gated via config and cluster-scoped FeatureFlag; opt-in rollout to a subset of dedicated fleets for two weeks, monitor p95/p99 latency and credit_reconcile_failure_count, then widen. Runbook contains rollback steps to revoke warmup leases and disable credit exchange globally.

release_notes: - Introduces the "warmup credit exchange" broker to allow tenants to borrow reserved warm slots for short bursts with automatic reconciliation. - Adds a burst cooldown controller that gradually cools a tenant's burst allowance to avoid oscillation and reactive overprovisioning. - Exposes per-tenant headroom metrics (p50/p95/allocated) and credit flow telemetry for SLO debugging.
